solution:
The wrong pair is (4) Chandrashekhar - Mandal Commission.

The chapter states that the commission to study the issue of the other backward classes was constituted in 1978 under the chairmanship of B. P. Mandal, while about Chandra Shekhar it says only that he became the Prime Minister of India in 1990 and that his government was short-lived. So the Mandal Commission is not connected with Chandra Shekhar.

The other three pairs are correctly matched. The National Emergency was declared during the tenure of Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi tried to make several reforms in the field of science and technology, and the government of P. V. Narasimha Rao initiated many changes and reforms in the Indian economy.

Chronological chart of the Prime Ministers named in this chapter:

| Prime Minister | Tenure as given in the chapter |
|---|---|
| Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru | Led the country after India became independent; he passed away in 1964 |
| Lal Bahadur Shastri | Succeeded Nehru in 1964; he breathed his last at Tashkent in 1966 |
| Indira Gandhi | Became the Prime Minister of India in 1966 |
| Morarji Desai | Became Prime Minister after the general elections that followed the Emergency of 1975-1977; his Janata Party government could not last long |
| Charan Singh | Succeeded Morarji Desai; his government too was a short-lived one |
| Indira Gandhi (second time) | Came to power again after the elections of 1980; she was assassinated in 1984 |
| Rajiv Gandhi | Became Prime Minister right after Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984; the Congress party was defeated in the elections of 1989 |
| Vishwanath Pratap Singh | Became Prime Minister after the 1989 elections at the head of the Janata Dal; he could not continue due to internal differences in the party |
| Chandra Shekhar | Became Prime Minister in 1990; his government was also short-lived |
| P. V. Narasimha Rao | His government started the economic reforms from 1991 |
| Atal Bihari Vajpayee, H. D. Devegowda, Inder Kumar Gujral | Worked as Prime Ministers during the period of the elections conducted between 1996 and 1999, when no party got a clear majority |
| Atal Bihari Vajpayee | Became Prime Minister in 1999 when the National Democratic Alliance came to power under the flag of the Bharatiya Janata Party |

[Note: the chapter does not state the exact starting and ending years of the tenure of every Prime Minister, so the description given in the chapter is written in place of such years.]

The changes that came about in India after 1991 are also described as globalisation. Globalisation brought about many changes in different fields like economy, politics, science and technology, and society and culture. Because of it India has emerged as an important country on the global scene in different spheres and is an important member of international organisations like G-20 and BRICS. India has experienced an important revolution in the field of telecommunication technology, and mobile phones, internet and communication facilities based on satellite have spread all across the country. In the political field India has demonstrated to the world how a stable democracy can function successfully. All this has resulted in a total transformation in the lifestyle of Indians, especially of the youth, which is visible from their dietary habits, clothing, language and beliefs.

The White Revolution is the name given to the great increase in milk production in India. It was the result of the experiment in the co-operative dairy movement carried out by Dr. Verghese Kurien. This experiment led to a large increase in the production of milk in the country. The chapter mentions the White Revolution along with the Green Revolution as one of the two major events that must be mentioned while describing India's efforts towards self-reliance.

On the backdrop of the Emergency, many opposition parties came together and formed a new party called the Janata Party. This newly formed party roundly defeated the Congress party led by Indira Gandhi in the general elections held after the Emergency, and Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister. But the Janata Party was made up of several different parties that had only recently come together, and internal differences soon arose in it. Because of these internal differences the Janata Party government under the leadership of Morarji Desai could not last long. Charan Singh, who succeeded him, also had a short-lived government, and fresh elections had to be conducted in 1980.

During the decade of the 1980s the Sikhs in Punjab demanded an independent state of Khalistan and began a movement for it. This movement went on to become violent and destructive, and Pakistan had lent its support to it. Terrorists had allegedly taken shelter in the Golden Temple at Amritsar, which is a holy shrine of the Sikhs. Therefore, in 1984, the Indian army had to be sent into the Golden Temple to evict these terrorists.

Right from independence, the modernisation of the economy, economic self-sufficiency and social justice have been the characteristics of the Indian economy. India wanted to acquire modernity and self-reliance by establishing industries. We also wanted to establish an economy based on social justice through planning. For this purpose the National Planning Commission was set up, so that it would coordinate development through the policy of Five Year Plans. The establishment of the Planning Commission, along with the emphasis on industrialisation, was a means to achieve economic development and to eliminate poverty in India.

The year 1991 is held to be very important in the history of the world as well as of India.

In world history, the Soviet Russia disintegrated into several different small countries in this year. Along with this, the Cold War came to an end.

In India, the government under the leadership of Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao initiated many changes in the Indian economy. This government started economic reforms from 1991, and these economic reforms are called economic liberalisation. As a result of the implementation of this policy the Indian economy flourished and the foreign investment in India increased. Skilled Indian professionals helped to reform the Indian economy, and the field of information technology opened several avenues of employment in the country. The changes that came about after 1991 are also described as globalisation. In this same year 1991, Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by the terrorist organisation of Sri Lanka, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), during an election campaign. For all these reasons 1991 was a year of important changes.

India wanted to acquire modernity and self-reliance by establishing industries. We wanted to establish an economy based on social justice through planning. For this the National Planning Commission was established, which would coordinate development through the policy of Five Year Plans. The establishment of the Planning Commission and the emphasis on industrialisation were a means to achieve economic development and to eliminate poverty in India.

From 1991 the Narasimha Rao government started economic reforms, which are called economic liberalisation. The Indian economy flourished as a result of the implementation of this policy and the foreign investment in India increased. Skilled Indian professionals helped to reform the Indian economy, and the field of information technology opened several avenues of employment in the country. The changes after 1991 are also described as globalisation.
